title: Overview of representation theory: associative algebras, representations, subrepresentations, direct sums

claims.claim: Representation theory studies representations of associative algebras.
claims.reason: This is a description of the subject's scope, not a mathematical proposition with a specified truth condition.

claims.claim: A unital associative algebra over a field is a vector space with associative bilinear multiplication and a two-sided identity.
The endomorphisms of a vector space form an associative algebra.
Algebras given by generators and relations, group algebras, and universal enveloping algebras are associative-algebra constructions.
A representation of A is a vector space V with a unital algebra homomorphism A → End(V), equivalently a left A-module.
A subrepresentation is a linear subspace invariant under every operator in the representation.
The direct sum of two representations carries the componentwise representation structure.

claims.claim: Representations of U(sl(2)) may be presented equivalently as Lie action maps of sl(2).
For every positive dimension d there exists an irreducible complex sl(2)-representation of dimension d.

title: Representations of group algebras k[G]
fidelity_note: The book claims a representation of the group algebra A = k[G] is "the same thing" as a representation of G, i.e. a vector space V with a group homomorphism rho : G -> GL(V). Formalized as two genuine bijections (Equiv), replacing the prior vacuous tautology Module k[G] V -> Module k[G] V. repEquivAlgHom: Representation k G V is equiv to (k[G] -> _a[k] Module.End k V), i.e. a representation of G is the same data as an algebra homomorphism out of k[G] (= a k-compatible k[G]-module structure on V). repEquivGL: Representation k G V is equiv to (G ->* (V ~=_l[k] V)), i.e. the same data as a group homomorphism rho : G -> GL(V) into the general linear group of invertible linear maps; invertibility is automatic because G is a group. Characterizing simp/rfl lemmas (repEquivAlgHom_apply_single, repEquivGL_apply, repEquivGL_symm_apply) pin down that the bijections are the intended maps (rho g acts as rho g), not arbitrary relabellings.

title: End_A(A) = A^op
Infinite dimensional Schur lemma (Dixmier)
fidelity_note: [fidelity] Verified faithful (#7243). Countability hypothesis is genuine (hcard : Module.rank ℂ V ≤ Cardinal.aleph0), NOT FiniteDimensional — the statement is strictly more general than finite Schur and non-vacuous. Irreducibility is [IsSimpleModule A V]. Conclusion asserts a genuine scalar operator (∃ c : ℂ, ∀ v, φ v = c • v) for φ : V →ₗ[A] V (A-linear homomorphism of representations), not merely commutation nor a weak existential. Ground field is ℂ literally: the transcendence/uncountability argument (Cardinal.mk_complex, aleph0_lt_continuum) is load-bearing. Axiom-clean: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], no sorryAx.
coverage_note: Formalized (#5884) in Chapter2/Problem2_3_18.lean as Etingof.Problem_2_3_18: for a ℂ-algebra A and an irreducible A-module V with Module.rank ℂ V ≤ ℵ₀, every φ : V →ₗ[A] V is scalar (∃ c, ∀ v, φ v = c • v). Proof follows Etingof's hint: D = Module.End A V is a division ring (Module.End.instDivisionRing / Schur); D is countably dimensional via injective ℂ-linear evaluation D → V at a nonzero vector; a non-scalar φ is transcendental over ℂ (else minpoly has degree 1 since ℂ is algebraically closed and D is a domain); the field ℂ(φ) is realized as the double centralizer Subalgebra.centralizer ℂ (Set.centralizer {φ}) (a commutative division subring, hence IsField.toField), inside which Transcendental.linearIndependent_sub_inv gives the uncountable ℂ-linearly independent family {(φ-a)⁻¹}, transported to D along the injective inclusion; then 𝔠 = #ℂ ≤ rank ℂ D ≤ ℵ₀ contradicts ℵ₀ < 𝔠. #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

title: Section 2.4 Ideals — heading and definitions

claims.claim: Left ideals, right ideals, and two-sided ideals have the stated closure conditions.
Left ideals are subrepresentations of the regular representation.
Right ideals are subrepresentations of the regular representation of the opposite algebra.
A two-sided ideal is simultaneously a left and a right ideal.
The zero ideal and the whole ring are two-sided ideals, and a nonzero ring with no others is simple.
The kernel of an algebra homomorphism is a two-sided ideal.
The two-sided ideal generated by S is the smallest such ideal and is the additive span of products a*s*b.
The left and right ideals generated by S are the corresponding one-sided spans.

claims.claim: For canonical multiplicity spaces V_X = Hom_A(X,V) and U_X = Hom_A(X,U), there is a natural linear isomorphism Hom_A(V,U) ≅ ∏_X Hom_k(V_X,U_X).
The isomorphism sends f to the component maps f_X given by post-composition, g ↦ f ∘ g.
An A-linear map f is injective if and only if every multiplicity-space component f_X is injective.
An A-linear map f is surjective if and only if every multiplicity-space component f_X is surjective.
An A-linear map f is an isomorphism if and only if every multiplicity-space component f_X is an isomorphism.
The Hom-space identification is natural: identity and composition become identity and componentwise composition.
The alternative argument is credited to B. Poonen.

title: Proof of Theorem 3.3.1 using dual representations
coverage_note: The complete advertised dual route is public: the transpose equivalence, twisted dual action, free-to-dual surjection, dual injection, regular and free-module decompositions, and final direct-sum classification are all formalized end to end.

claims.claim: Each standard V_i is irreducible; a matrix element can send any chosen nonzero vector to any target vector.

claims.claim: For finite-dimensional X, the dual X* is finite-dimensional of the same dimension.
Matrix transpose identifies Mat_d(k) with its opposite algebra because (BC)^T = C^T B^T.
Applying transpose factorwise identifies A = ⊕_i Mat_{d_i}(k) with A^op.
Using the transpose anti-automorphism, X* is again an A-representation.
A basis y_l of X* defines the A-linear map φ : A^n → X* by φ(a) = ∑_l a_l y_l.
The map φ is surjective because scalar coefficients embed from k into A.
Dualizing φ gives an injective A-linear map X → (A^n)*.
The dual of A^n is A-linearly isomorphic to A^n.
The regular representation decomposes as A ≃ ⊕_i d_i V_i.
The free representation A^n decomposes as ⊕_i (n d_i) V_i.
The image of X in A^n is a subrepresentation to which Proposition 3.1.4 applies.
Consequently X is A-linearly isomorphic to ⊕_i m_i V_i for suitable multiplicities m_i.

title: Adjacency matrix of graph with nonabelian automorphism group has repeated eigenvalues
coverage_note: Proved in EtingofRepresentationTheory/Chapter4/Problem4_12_4.lean via the spectral theorem: squarefree charpoly ⟹ distinct eigenvalues ⟹ commutant of the adjacency matrix is commutative, so the permutation matrices of two graph automorphisms commute, contradicting nonabelianness.
fidelity_note: [fidelity] VERIFIED (#7265). Hypothesis '∃ σ τ : Γ ≃g Γ, σ * τ ≠ τ * σ' is exactly 'automorphism group nonabelian': Γ ≃g Γ (= RelIso Γ.Adj Γ.Adj) is the graph automorphism group with a Group instance, mul is composition ((σ*τ) x = σ (τ x)), and ∃ non-commuting pair = negation of commutativity. Conclusion '¬ Squarefree (Γ.adjMatrix ℝ).charpoly' faithfully encodes 'repeated eigenvalue': adjMatrix is real symmetric (IsHermitian), so charpoly_eq splits it as ∏(X - C λ_i) with λ_i real, whence ¬Squarefree ⟺ eigenvalues not distinct ⟺ repeated real eigenvalue (neither over- nor under-stated). Non-vacuous: hypothesis satisfiable (K₃ has Aut = S₃, nonabelian); empty/singleton W forces trivial Aut so W is genuinely populated wherever hAut holds. sorry-free, axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

source_span: $\sigma(\rho) \leq \rho$ lexicographically with equality if and only if $\sigma = 1$, and subtracting both sides from the constant vector $\lambda + \rho$ shows that $\lambda + \rho - \sigma(\rho) \geq \lambda$ with equality if and only if $\sigma = 1$.
claim: For sigma in S_N acting on rho = (N-1, N-2, ..., 0): sigma(rho) <=_lex rho with equality iff sigma = 1; equivalently lambda + rho - sigma(rho) >=_lex lambda with equality iff sigma = 1.
note: Stage 3.7 reconciliation (audit #7245): covered_full. Both directions formalized: the lex inequality σ(ρ)≤ρ on the staircase ρ=(N−1,…,0) (rhoVec_comp_perm_le) AND the load-bearing equality-iff-identity (rhoVec_comp_perm_eq_iff, an actual ↔ σ=1), plus the equivalent λ+ρ−σ(ρ)≥λ form with its own equality-iff-identity (laVec_eq_shifted_sub_perm_iff). Proved via the least-non-fixed-point argument, not assumed. Sorry-free. Status accepted→sorry_free. Same claim reused by Chapter5/Discussion_proof_of_Frobenius_character_formula; formalization lives in this footnote file. (Prior issue #5682.)

source_span: It is easy to show that if F is an additive functor, then F(X ⊕ Y) is canonically isomorphic to F(X) ⊕ F(Y).
claim: An additive functor F between preadditive categories with biproducts satisfies F(X ⊞ Y) ≅ F(X) ⊞ F(Y) canonically.
note: Derived items are keyed by `derived_from`, not `id` (per PLAN Stage 1.6) — the empty-id flag in audit #7001 was a false positive. Etingof.AdditiveFunctor.mapBiprod_hom proved sorry-free; #print axioms: propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only. Status bumped formalized→sorry_free in audit #7001.

source_span: Note that in a semisimple category, any additive functor is automatically exact on both sides.
claim: For a semisimple abelian category C (every short exact sequence splits), any additive functor F : C → D is both left and right exact.
note: Stage 3.7 reconciliation (audit #7245): covered_full. IsSemisimpleCategory faithfully = "every short exact sequence splits"; conclusion (S.map F).ShortExact is genuine two-sided exactness (mono+epi+middle-exact). Proof genuinely consumes semisimplicity (extracts splitting, pushes through F via F.Additive) — quantified over all short exact S, not just split ones. Sorry-free. Status accepted→sorry_free. (Prior issue #5684.)

source_span: Show that if V is an irreducible complex representation of a finite group G of dimension > 1, then there exists g \in G such that \chi_V(g) = 0.
claim: For an irreducible complex representation V of a finite group G with dim V > 1, there exists g with χ_V(g) = 0 (Problem 5.2.7 part (b)).
